:::{#sol-log-partition-derivative}

The left side of @exr-log-partition-normalization is a function of $\natparam$ alone,
and its derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dif{\expf{\logpartitionf{\natparam}}}{\natparam}
&= \expf{\logpartitionf{\natparam}} \, \dif{\logpartitionf{\natparam}}{\natparam}
&& \text{(chain rule)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative of the right side moves inside the integral,
where only the exponential depends on $\natparam$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dif{}{\natparam} \int \basemeasuref{\rvar} \, \expf{\natparam \, \statf{\rvar}} \, d\rvar
&= \int \basemeasuref{\rvar} \, \dif{\expf{\natparam \, \statf{\rvar}}}{\natparam} \, d\rvar
&& \text{(the derivative of the integral is the integral of the derivative)}\\
&= \int \basemeasuref{\rvar} \, \statf{\rvar} \, \expf{\natparam \, \statf{\rvar}} \, d\rvar
&& \text{(chain rule)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the two derivatives and solving for the derivative of the log-partition function:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dif{\logpartitionf{\natparam}}{\natparam}
&= \expf{-\logpartitionf{\natparam}} \int \basemeasuref{\rvar} \, \statf{\rvar} \, \expf{\natparam \, \statf{\rvar}} \, d\rvar
&& \text{(divide both sides by } \expf{\logpartitionf{\natparam}} \text{)}\\
&= \int \statf{\rvar} \, \basemeasuref{\rvar} \, \expf{\natparam \, \statf{\rvar}} \, \expf{-\logpartitionf{\natparam}} \, d\rvar
&& \text{(a factor free of the integration variable moves into the integral)}\\
&= \int \statf{\rvar} \, \basemeasuref{\rvar} \, \expf{\natparam \, \statf{\rvar} - \logpartitionf{\natparam}} \, d\rvar
&& \text{(the product of exponentials is the exponential of the sum)}\\
&= \int \statf{\rvar} \, \pdf\paren{\rvar ; \natparam} \, d\rvar
&& \text{(@eq-exponential-family)}\\
&= \E{\statf{\Rvar}}
&& \text{(definition of the expectation)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
